items.claim: The National Education Foundation (founded 2000) runs Global Academy of Technology, Global College of Nursing and National Hill View Public School; its own site lists Usha Shivakumar as Chairperson, D.K. Shivakumar and D.K. Suresh as trustees, and Aishwarya DKS Hegde as Secretary Trustee.
items.quote: Smt. Aishwarya DKS Hegde – Secretary Trustee
items.note: Spellings vary: Aishwarya / Aisshwarya / Aishwarya DKS Hegde. GAT governing body page also lists her as Trustee Secretary.

items.claim: At a Karnataka government CSR event on school adoption, NEF trustee-secretary Aishwarya Shivakumar said low efficiency, more than teacher shortage, was the problem, and that some teachers earning about Rs 1.1 lakh did not attend regularly.
items.quote: More than teacher shortage, low efficiency is the problem
items.note: Exact date and venue not stated in the report. The CM launched the 'Namma Shaale Namma Javabdari' CSR programme in Bengaluru on Wed 4 Nov 2026 (Careers360, 5 Nov): likely but NOT confirmed to be the same event. She also said private funders should be able to monitor staff attendance and performance.

items.claim: JD(S) MLC A.P. Ranganath (Bangalore Teachers' constituency) said the remarks undermined teachers' dignity and asked her to apologise; the Save Public Education Committee, AIDSO and the RTE Students Parents Association opposed the school-adoption plan.
items.quote: Private education may be a choice, but public education is a constitutional and social responsibility
items.note: No formal government response beyond the CM saying his own criticism (teachers earning about Rs 1.5 lakh) did not apply to all teachers. No named teachers' union statement found. UNI (7 Nov) names her 'Aishwarya DKS Hegde' and says teachers' organisations questioned the blame; full UNI text paywalled.

items.claim: Launching the CSR school programme, CM Shivakumar said government school teachers are paid between Rs 70,000 and Rs 1.5 lakh a month and that the quality of education still needs to improve.
items.quote: the quality of education still needs to improve
items.note: He asked private institutions to support 1,000 rural government schools.

items.claim: On 12 September 2019 the Enforcement Directorate questioned Aishwarya, then 22, for over seven hours in Delhi and recorded her statement under PMLA in the money-laundering case against her father; she was described as a trustee of an education trust he set up.
items.quote: Aishwarya is a trustee in an education trust floated by her father.
items.note: She was questioned as part of the probe; nothing found shows she was ever charged in it. Do not describe her as an accused.

items.claim: On 5 March 2024 the Supreme Court (Justices Surya Kant and K.V. Viswanathan) quashed the ED's PMLA proceedings against D.K. Shivakumar, applying its Pavana Dibbur ruling; it said the ED may seek recall if that ruling is reviewed.
items.quote: the proceedings initiated against the appellants under the PMLA are hereby quashed
items.note: Quashed on a legal point (a conspiracy charge alone is not a scheduled offence). Not an acquittal on facts and not a finding of guilt.

items.claim: The Income Tax Department's prosecution of D.K. Shivakumar arising from 2017 raids (CC 30798/2021) was still pending before a Bengaluru magistrate court in May 2026; related Supreme Court petitions had stayed proceedings.
items.quote: the personal presence of accused in this case may not be required until further orders
items.note: Article partly paywalled. Status after the 10 June 2026 hearing not found. No conviction exists.

items.claim: The Supreme Court on 15 July 2024 dismissed Shivakumar's plea to quash the CBI disproportionate-assets case registered on 3 October 2020.
items.quote: dismissed his plea for quashing the CBI case related to possession of disproportionate assets
items.note: Later status (including litigation over the state's 2023 withdrawal of CBI consent) not verified. A pending case, no finding.

items.claim: In February 2023 the CBI served a notice on Aishwarya, trustee secretary of NEF; according to her father, it sought fee and academic details.
items.quote: information regarding how much fees have been paid, what exams she passed
items.note: The description is Shivakumar's own account; purpose not independently confirmed.

items.claim: UDISE+ 2025-26: 37.8% of Karnataka's government schools (18,330 of 48,527) have computers for teaching, against 84.3% of private schools.
items.quote: Among government-run schools, 18,330, or 37.8 per cent, have computers for teaching purposes
items.note: An unnamed official said data entry was still in progress and newer figures would differ. UDISE+ tables themselves not opened.

items.claim: In a written Assembly reply on 18 Dec 2025, the education minister said 45,590 of 1,78,935 sanctioned teacher posts in 41,088 government primary schools were vacant (25.5%); in 5,024 government high schools, 12,134 of 44,144 posts were vacant.
items.quote: Of these, 1,33,345 posts have been filled, while 45,590 posts remain vacant.
items.note: 25.5% is our arithmetic (45,590 / 1,78,935). 51,000 guest teachers appointed for 2025-26.

items.claim: The school education minister told the Assembly that enrolment in Karnataka government schools fell by 17 lakh over the past 15 years.
items.quote: Enrolment in government-run schools in Karnataka has dropped by 17 lakh over the past 15 years.
items.note: A 15-year span, not 10; start and end years not named. 309 Karnataka Public Schools set up so far.

items.claim: The government plans KPS-Magnet schools into which nearby schools are merged; a state list identifies 474 government schools for merger. The government says no school will be closed; AIDSO alleges over 40,000 will be.
items.quote: Not a single school in the state will be closed.
items.note: 40,000 is an unverified AIDSO allegation and must be attributed. No official count of closed or merged schools found.

items.claim: In 2024-25, 6,158 Karnataka government schools had only one teacher, serving about 1.38 lakh students (down from 6,360 in 2023-24).
items.note: Conflicting counts: UDISE+ 2024-25 reportedly 7,349 (possibly all managements); DH reports 6,675 for 2025-26 vs 5,412 (DH blocked, snippet only). Cite one source by name if used.

items.claim: Karnataka budgeted Rs 44,054 crore for education, sports, arts and culture in 2026-27, up from Rs 34,210 crore actually spent in 2024-25; PRS puts the sector at about 11% of spending.
items.quote: Education, Sports, Arts, and Culture 34,210 40,954 39,642 44,054 11%
items.note: On PRS numbers the share is roughly flat (about 10-11%), not a clear decline. DH says the share fell, but the article could not be opened. Long-run trend not verified.

items.claim: B.S. Yediyurappa formally resigned as Chief Minister on 31 July 2011, handing his resignation to Governor H.R. Bhardwaj, after Lokayukta Santosh Hegde's report on illegal mining named him.
items.quote: submitted his resignation officially
items.note: Report submitted 27 July 2011 per timelines (not separately opened). The report's bribe claim (Rs 20 crore via a family trust) was an allegation.

items.claim: On 26 October 2016 a special CBI court acquitted Yediyurappa, his sons, his son-in-law and others in the CBI mining/Prerana Trust case, saying the prosecution failed to prove a conspiracy.
items.quote: failed to prove that there was a meeting of mind

items.claim: Private complaints filed in 2011 over land denotification led to Yediyurappa spending 24 days in judicial custody; on 4 Dec 2018 the Supreme Court threw out five such cases.
items.quote: did not stand scrutiny of the law
items.note: Custody began 15 Oct 2011 after the Lokayukta court rejected bail (seen in Business Standard snippets; page blocked). The SC stayed another denotification case on 5 Apr 2021 (TNM); its final status not found.

items.claim: The CBI arrested G. Janardhan Reddy on 5 Sept 2011; he spent nearly three and a half years in jail before the Supreme Court granted bail on 20 Jan 2015. On 6 May 2025 a special CBI court in Hyderabad sentenced him to seven years in the Obulapuram Mining case, registered in 2009.
items.quote: seven years' rigorous imprisonment
items.note: Case registered 8 Dec 2009, verdict May 2025: about 15.5 years. Sabitha Indra Reddy acquitted.

items.claim: On 11 June 2025 the Telangana High Court suspended Reddy's conviction and sentence and granted bail pending appeal.
items.quote: suspended the conviction and sentence awarded to former Karnataka minister Gali Janardhan Reddy
items.note: Appeal outcome not found.

items.claim: On 26 Oct 2024 a Bengaluru special court for elected representatives sentenced Karwar MLA Satish Sail to seven years over the theft and export of seized iron ore from Belekeri (2009-10).
items.quote: sentenced Karwar MLA Satish Krishna Sail to seven years in prison
items.note: The fine is reported variously (Rs 15 crore, or Rs 44 crore total across the accused).

items.claim: On 13 Nov 2024 the Karnataka High Court suspended Sail's sentence, on condition that 25% of the penalty is deposited within six weeks.
items.quote: The sentence will remain suspended provided this condition is fulfilled.
items.note: Appeal outcome not found.

items.claim: According to a government reply in the Legislative Council, the Karnataka Lokayukta registered 1,248 corruption cases from Sept 2022 to Aug 2026; 364 were chargesheeted, 648 were under investigation and 218 faced court stays.
items.note: Organiser also says no government employee was declared guilty although 148 judgments were delivered. That looks internally odd; check against the Council reply before using the conviction line.

items.claim: NCRB Crime in India 2024 recorded 334 corruption cases in Karnataka, third highest after Maharashtra and Tamil Nadu.
items.note: Karnataka's 2024 PC Act conviction rate and pendency not found in any opened source.

items.claim: Under the Karnataka Lokayukta Act, any person may complain to the Lokayukta or an Upalokayukta through a statement backed by an affidavit; a false and frivolous or vexatious complaint is punishable with six months to three years in jail.
items.quote: any person may make a complaint under this Act to the Lokayukta or an Upalokayukta
items.note: Sec 9(1),(2); Sec 20. Rules: Form I plus Form II affidavit, filed in person or by registered post to the Registrar (legitquest copy of the 1986 amendment rules). Filing fee not confirmed.

items.claim: Section 22 of the Lokayukta Act requires MLAs and other non-government public servants to file assets and liabilities for themselves and their family before 30 June every year; defaulters are reported and, after two more months, named in three newspapers.
items.quote: before the 30th June of every year submit to the Lokayukta
items.note: Section 22 sets no fine or jail penalty for not filing.

items.claim: In November 2025 the Lokayukta flagged 100 legislators, including five ministers, 66 MLAs and 28 MLCs, for not filing 2024-25 asset statements; 30% of MLAs and 37% of MLCs had not declared.
items.quote: 30% of MLAs and 37% of MLCs
items.note: Counts differ across outlets (66 or 67 MLAs; parts don't sum to 100). The 30% figure is the safest to quote. No 2025-26 list found.

items.claim: Karnataka's RTI rules set an application fee of Rs 10, payable by postal order, demand draft, banker's cheque or treasury remittance; copies cost Rs 2 per A4 page.
items.note: The CHRI page dates from about 2008. BPL exemption not confirmed in an opened source (central RTI Act s.7(5) exempts BPL applicants).

items.claim: Under the Karnataka Gram Swaraj and Panchayat Raj Act, a Ward Sabha must meet once every six months and may get information from the gram panchayat on the rationale of every decision affecting its ward; it identifies beneficiaries for welfare schemes.
items.quote: to get information from the Gram Panchayat on the rationale of every decision
items.note: Sec 3C/3D. Quorum: the lesser of one-fifth of voters or 20. Gram Sabha frequency (s.3G) not read; secondary sources say at least once in six months. Urban ward committees and area sabhas not covered.
